assumptions: The literal 'missing_mass': 1.0 field is treated as a coarse/placeholder indicator rather than a directly usable estimate; the working missing-mass estimate below is instead derived from coverage_low/coverage_high (implying ~84%-96.5% unseen mass) and cross-checked against the Chao1 gap ((595-34)/595 ≈ 94%), since these two independent signals converge and the raw field does not.

Slot vocabularies are judged 'incomplete' based on evidence-coverage thinness (only 8 evidence items from 3 sources feeding 34 generated / 8 surviving hypotheses) relative to how many distinct values each slot actually exhibits in the frontier, not on any external ground-truth vocabulary size.

The target-blind 'rate: 0.0' is assumed to mean the proportion of surviving hypotheses that proposed a non-consensus (non-anchor) actor or mechanism value, consistent with meta_review's observation that mechanism never varies and actor is dominated by alpha-team/alpha-observatory across the frontier.

Because prior_rate is None and first_run is True, 'steady: True' is assumed to be a vacuous default emitted by the pipeline in the absence of a prior run to compare against, not an evidenced measurement of stability.
No training-derived (model-prior) claims about comets, orbital tracking, or historical observatories were used to interpret this run; all judgments are drawn strictly from the supplied run data.
incomplete_vocabularies: mechanism — only a single value (transit-timing-method) appears across all 8 surviving hypotheses; the meta_review explicitly flags this as structurally unexamined, so the slot's vocabulary is effectively a vocabulary of one and cannot be considered sampled at all.

actor — heavily skewed to alpha-team (5/8) and alpha-observatory (7/8), with only two genuinely new actor values added this run (independent-review-body, press-release-media-source), both derived from single evidence items (gt-gamma-downgrade, gt-beta-contested); no rival named-actor branch (e.g., beta-team) has been evidentially tested, so the observed actor set is dominated by one anchor cluster plus thin singleton additions.

interval — effectively binary in practice (narrow [1950,1950] tied to the anchor vs. wide [1900,1999] fallback everywhere else), with no alternate narrow intervals or isolated single-slot tests of interval independent of the anchor's other fixed slots, per the meta_review's 'confounded interval' flag.
response.calibration_summary: This run shows moderate internal robustness (7/8 survivors, i.e. 0.875, rated stable) but weak probabilistic calibration: a Brier score of 0.327 is worse than a trivial constant-0.5 baseline (0.25) on a balanced outcome set, and with only 8 survivors and a single anchor-dominated cluster (alpha-team/alpha-observatory/comet-q present in the large majority of hypotheses, all seven non-anchor branches sitting at u=1.0/b=0/d=0), the surprise rate of 0.125 is almost certainly measuring one hypothesis against an otherwise unevaluated, evidence-starved population rather than a genuinely tested distribution — so both the Brier score and surprise rate should be read as low-confidence, small-n signals until an evidence-gathering pass converts some of the seven u=1.0 branches into genuine b>0 or d>0 readings.
response.target_blind_note: Reported steady=True, but this is the campaign's first run (first_run=True, prior_rate=None), so there is no actual prior baseline to compare against — the flag is vacuously true rather than an evidenced stability signal. What is concerning independent of steadiness is the absolute value: the non-consensus actor/mechanism proposal rate is 0.0, matching the meta_review's structural finding that mechanism never varies (transit-timing-method in 8/8) and actor is dominated by the alpha-team/alpha-observatory anchor cluster — i.e., generation is currently a single-slot ablation sweep around one base claim with effectively zero exploration of rival actors or mechanisms. This 0.0 rate should be treated as the true baseline to watch: if the next run under similar evidence volume also lands at or near 0.0, that would indicate the generator is structurally incapable of proposing non-consensus actor/mechanism values rather than merely 'holding steady' in a healthy sense — a falling-or-flat-at-zero rate here is the analogous failure mode to a collapsing surprise rate, and warrants the same scrutiny once a second data point exists.
